lessons.title: The body
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Leo stretch and exercise in the gym.

items.note: Use 'head' for the top part of your body where your face and hair are.

image.describe: a friendly black cat pointing to its head in a gym

items.note: Use 'arm' for the long part of your body from your shoulder to your hand.

image.describe: a cat stretching one arm up high

items.note: Use 'leg' for the part of your body that you use to walk and run.

image.describe: a cat lifting its leg while exercising

items.note: Use 'hand' for the part at the end of your arm with fingers.

image.describe: a close up of a cat holding out an open hand

items.note: Use 'foot' for the part at the bottom of your leg that stands on the ground.

image.describe: a cat showing its foot on the gym floor

items.note: Use 'back' for the rear part of your body from your shoulders to your hips.

image.describe: a cat stretching its back on a gym mat

grammar.title: Body parts
grammar.explanation: Use singular nouns like head, arm, leg, hand, foot, and back to name parts of the body.

practice.prompt: Which word means the top part of your body?
practice.explanation: Head is the top part of your body.

practice.explanation: The audio says leg.

practice.explanation: This is my hand is correct.

practice.prompt: Match the words with their meanings.
practice.explanation: Head, foot, and back are important body parts.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Say: This is my back.

story.hook: What is Smarty doing in the gym?

image.describe: Smarty the cat and Leo are in a bright gym doing morning stretches.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello, Leo! Let us stretch.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Okay, Smarty. I can move my head and my arm.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good! Now lift your leg and tap your foot.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: And stretch your back, too!

mission.setup: Smarty asks you to name a body part you are moving.

items.note: Use 'eye' for the part of your face that you use to see.

image.describe: a cat blinking one eye

items.note: Use 'nose' for the part on your face that you use to smell.

items.note: Use 'mouth' for the part of your face that you use to speak and eat.

items.note: Use 'tooth' for the hard white parts inside your mouth; more than one is 'teeth'.

items.note: Use 'neck' for the part of your body that connects your head to your shoulders.

image.describe: a cat turning its neck

grammar.title: Face and head parts
grammar.explanation: Use eye, ear, nose, mouth, tooth, and neck to talk about your face and head.

lessons.title: Good advice
lessons.scenario: Smarty talks to Sam about staying healthy.

items.note: Say 'You should' to give good advice or recommend an action.
Say 'You should not' to advise someone against doing something.
Say 'Take a rest' when you need to stop working and relax.

items.example: Stay in bed when you are ill.
items.note: Say 'Stay in bed' when resting at home.

items.example: Drink more water in the gym.
items.note: Say 'Drink more water' to stay hydrated.

items.example: I am tired, so I will rest.
items.note: Use 'so' to connect a reason with a result.

grammar.title: should and should not
grammar.explanation: Use 'You should' for good actions and 'You should not' for actions to avoid. Use 'so' to show results.

lessons.title: Staying healthy

items.note: Use 'healthy' when your body is strong and well.

items.example: Eat a balanced diet with fruit and vegetables.

Say 'I need to rest' when you must stop and relax.
